thread:
alex: heads-up  healthtech pilot wants a shorter commit (90 days) and a hard monthly token ceiling per tenant. also asked for an option to opt into 30d data retention on Dedicated and an enterprise p95 SLA. GTM needs a clear packaging decision by EOD Fri.

jen: sales recap: they9re effectively asking for: (1) 3mo reserved commit with conversion option, (2) a microtier capped at 50M tokens/mo with optional burst top-ups, (3) a 30d retention add-on for dedicated deployments, and (4) an SLA for p95 <= 150ms for text-gen under their expected concurrency.

maria: what9s restrictive here technically is the 30d retention toggle. cutting retention from 90->30d kills long prefix caching and increases backend cost. we need a delta estimate.

finance: quick finance note  removing 60d of cache increases our opcost for that tenant by ~10% given their call pattern. a 3mo short commit at a higher $/token can cover the risk.

eng-platform: enforcement question: do we implement token ceilings as a hard reject at the routing layer or as a billing-enforced cutoff? hard reject is safer for customers that want limits, but requires changes to quota service + request path checks. estimate: 2w dev + 1w QA. billing-only enforcement is easier (1w) but customer gets surprise overages unless we block at UI/API.

sam: retention toggle work: tenant config flag + purge job + QA for cache isolation. estimate 1w. need to add telemetry: tenant cache-miss rate, token spend delta, purge job timings.

dylan-biz: revenue approaches I9m leaning to:
- Pilot approach: 3mo at +25% $/token, includes a clause to convert to 12mo at a fixed discount if they commit within the 3mo.
- Fixed microtier: normal list price but no conversion option.
We should model churn risk on pilot.

alex: we need packaging options to present at sync. draft three concise packages:
1) Pilot Reserve: 3mo premium, convertible to 12mo at discount; includes SLA only after conversion.
2) Microtier Cap: permanent microtier (50M/mo) with hard cap enforcement and optional prepaid burst credits; no retention change by default.
3) Retention Add-on: 30d retention for Dedicated as a billable add-on with explicit perf/regression caveat.

jen: customer will only sign if both the retention toggle and the p95 SLA exist. they9re unlikely to accept an SLA that9s gated on conversion to 12mo. need to confirm willingness to accept SLA on pilot vs only post-conversion.

legal: for short commits we9ll need a pilot clause: payment non-refundable for 3mo, early conversion credits, clear termination and data retention language (30d purge for add-on). include SOC2 and data handling language.

maria: engineering tradeoffs: if we offer SLA on pilot, ops needs the runbook and capacity reservation (dedicated pool) to hit p95. that9s non-trivial and requires autoscale guardrails. suggest we make SLA available only for dedicated reserved capacity (not shared hosted).

eng-platform: deploy-bot = load test scheduled 2026-04-02T22:00Z on dedicated-staging. we can use that to validate p95 under expected request mix; results in 24h.

alex: launch gating checklist proposal:
- infra: routing/quota changes in place for hard cap OR billing hook for top-ups
- infra: tenant retention flag + purge job with test coverage
- runtime: pass p95 <150ms on dedicated load test
- legal: pilot contract template (non-refundable 3mo + conversion path)
- billing: UI and invoice flows for burst top-ups and cap enforcement messages
- QA: smoke tests for cache isolation and telemetry dashboards added

sam: implementation plan (parallelizable):
- Week 0-1: retention flag + purge job (1 eng)
- Week 0-2: routing quota + hard-reject path (2 engs)
- Week 1: billing top-up MVP and invoice flow (1 eng)
- Week 2: end-to-end QA and runbook creation
If we staff 2 engs we can hit minimal viable in ~2w.

dylan-biz: action items for GTM: finance to provide delta model, legal to draft pilot template, eng to produce ETA doc, sales to confirm customer tolerance for pilot premium and SLA timing.

jen: I9ll confirm customer stance on pilot-SLA vs post-conversion SLA before EOD.

finance: I9ll push a 3-scenario sheet (pilot premium, microtier, retention add-on) by EOD Thu.

legal: will draft a short pilot contract (SOC2 + 30d purge clause) draft by Fri morning.

alex: good. if product sync agrees, we9ll ship Option 1 (Pilot Reserve) as a targeted offer with Option 2 & 3 available as add-ons inside 4 weeks. aim to close pilot with this customer as reference for short-commit product.

eng-platform: tagging follow-ups: eng estimate doc: https://redwood.internal/eng/estimates/2481 (placeholder), runbook stub, telemetry dashboards ticket.

alex: :+1: closing thread, will present at sync.
